items.title: Why So Many Temples?
items.hook: Kyoto kept the old capital’s job: houses for gods and for monks.
items.task: Count how many temple or shrine roofs you can see from one street.
items.reveal: Emperors sat here for centuries. Temples and shrines stacked up around the court.

moreInfo.title: A long capital
moreInfo.text: Kyoto was the imperial seat for about a thousand years. Power later moved. The religious houses stayed. Confirm the date range before live.

items.title: Shrine or Temple?
items.task: At the next holy place, decide: shrine or temple? Use what you can see.
items.physicalObservation: Torii, rope, foxes, incense, cemetery, Buddha.
items.reveal: Shrines are Shinto. Temples are Buddhist. The clues overlap. Guess, then check the name.
items.notes: Recurring. Do not teach one perfect checklist.

items.title: Spot the Pokémon Ancestor
items.task: Find a statue or picture of a Japanese creature: fox, raccoon-dog, water-child, crow-goblin or ogre.
items.reveal: Japan collected strange beings long before games. Pokémon borrowed a habit of cataloguing, not a one-to-one family tree.

moreInfo.title: Yōkai
moreInfo.text: Kitsune, tanuki, kappa, tengu and oni are old names. Do not say a game monster is the same being. The Codex category is folklore, not merch.

items.notes: Unlocks Yokai & Spirits as a category idea. Not a Pokémon license.
